source_text: Καὶ ὁ Τρύφων· Ἐμοὶ μὲν δοκοῦσιν, εἶπεν, οἱ λέγοντες ἄνθρωπον γεγονέναι αὐτὸν καὶ κατ᾿ ἐκλογὴν κεχρῖσθαι καὶ Χριστὸν γεγονέναι πιθανώτερον ὑμῶν λέγειν, τῶν ταῦτα ἅπερ φῂς λεγόντων· καὶ γὰρ πάντες ἡμεῖς τὸν Χριστὸν ἄνθρωπον ἐξ ἀνθρώπων προσδοκῶμεν γενήσεσθαι , καὶ τὸν Ἡλίαν χρῖσαι αὐτὸν ἐλθόντα. Ἐὰν δὲ οὗτος φαίνηται ὢν ὁ Χριστός, ἄνθρωπον μὲν ἐξ ἀνθρώπων γενόμενον ἐκ παντὸς ἐπίστασθαι δεῖ. Ἐκ δὲ τοῦ μηδὲ Ἡλίαν ἐληλυθέναι οὐδὲ τοῦτον ἀποφαίνομαι εἶναι. Κἀγὼ πάλιν ἐπυθόμην αὐτοῦ· Οὐχὶ Ἡλίαν φησὶν ὁ λόγος διὰ Ζαχαρίου ἐλεύσεσθαι πρὸ τῆς ἡμέρας τῆς μεγάλης καὶ φοβερᾶς ταύτης τοῦ κυρίου ; Κἀκεῖνος ἀπεκρίνατο· Μάλιστα. Ἐὰν οὖν ὁ λόγος ἀναγκάζῃ ὁμολογεῖν ὅτι δύο παρουσίαι τοῦ Χριστοῦ προεφητεύοντο γενησόμεναι, μία μέν. ἐν ᾖ παθητός καὶ ἄτιμος καὶ ἀειδὴς φανήσεται , ἡ δὲ ἑτέρα, ἐν ᾗ καὶ ἔνδοξος καὶ κριτὴς ἁπάντων ἐλεύσεται , ὡς καὶ ἐν πολλοῖς τοῖς προλελεγμένοις ἀποδέδεικται, οὐχὶ τῆς φοβερᾶς καὶ μεγάλης ἡμέρας τουτέστι τῆς δευτέρας παρουσίας αὐτοῦ, πρόοδον γενήσεσθαι τὸν Ἡλίαν νοήσομεν τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ κεκηρυχέναι; Μάλιστα, ἀπεκρίνατο. Καὶ ὁ ἡμέτερος οὖν κύριος, ἔφην, τοῦτο αὐτὸ ἐν τοῖς διδάγμασιν αὐτοῦ παρέδωκε γενησόμενον, εἰπὼν καὶ Ἡλίαν ἐλεύσεσθαι · καὶ ἡμεῖς τοῦτο ἐπιστάμεθα γενησόμενον, ὅταν μέλλῃ ἐν δόξῃ ἐξ οὐρανῶν παραγίνεσθαι ὁ ἡμέτερος κύριος Ἰησοῦς Χριστός, οὗ καὶ τῆς πρώτης φανερώσεως κῆρυξ προῆλθε τὸ ἐν Ἡλίᾳ γενόμενον πνεῦμα τοῦ θεοῦ, ἐν Ἰωάννῃ , τῷ γενομένῳ ἐν τῷ γένει ὑμῶν προφήτῃ, μεθ᾿ ὃν οὐδεὶς ἕτερος λοιπὸν παρ᾿ ὑμῖν ἐφάνη προφήτης· ὅστις ἐπὶ τὸν Ἰορδάνην ποταμὸν καθεζόμενος ἐβόα· Ἐγὼ μὲν ὑμᾶς βαπτίζω ὲν ὕδατι εἰς μετάνοιαν· ἥξει δὲ ὁ ἰσχυρότερός μου, οὗ οὐκ εἰμὶ ἱκανὸς τὰ ὑποδήματα βαστάσαι· αὐτὸς ὑμᾶς βαπτίσει ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ καὶ πυρί. Οὗ τὸ πτύον αὐτοῦ ἐν τῇ χειρὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ διακαθαριεῖ τὴν ἅλωνα αὐτοῦ καὶ τὸν σῖτον συνάξει εἰς τὴν ἀποθήκην, τὸ δὲ ἄχυρον κατακαύσει πυρὶ ἀσβέστῳ . Καὶ τοῦτον αὐτὸν τὸν προφήτην συνεκεκλείκει ὁ βασιλεὺς ὑμῶν Ἡρώδης εἰς φυλακήν. καὶ γενεσίων ἡμέρας τελουμένης, ὀρχουμένης τῆς ἐξαδελφῆς αὐτοῦ εὐαρέστως αὐτῷ, εἶπεν αὐτῇ αἰτήσασθαι ὃ ἐὰν βούληται. Καὶ ἡ μήτηρ τῆς παιδὸς ὑπέβαλεν αὐτῇ αἰτήσασθαι τὴν κεφαλὴν Ἰωάννου τοῦ ἐν τῇ φυλακῇ· καὶ αἰτησάσης ἔπεμψε καὶ ἐπὶ πίνακι ἐνεχθῆναι τὴν κεφαλὴν Ἰωάννου ἐκέλευσε . Διὸ καὶ ὁ ἡμέτερος Χριστὸς εἰρήκει ἐπὶ γῆς τότε τοῖς λέγουσι πρὸ τοῦ Χριστοῦ Ἡλίαν δεῖν ἐλθεῖν· Ἡλίας μὲν ἐλεύσεται καὶ ἀποκαταστήσει πάντα· λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι Ἡλίας ἤδη ἦλθε, καὶ οὐκ ἐπέγνωσαν αὐτόν, ἀλλ᾿ ἐποίησαν αὐτῷ ὅσα ἠθέλησαν. Καὶ γέγραπται ὅτι Τότε συνῆκαν οἱ μαθηταὶ ὅτι περὶ Ἰωάννου τοῦ βαπτιστοῦ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς . Καὶ ὁ Τρύφων· Καὶ τοῦτο παράδοξον λέγειν μοι δοκεῖς, ὅτι τὸ ἐν Ἡλίᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ γενόμενον προφητικὸν πνεῦμα καὶ ἐν Ἰωάννῃ γέγονε. Κἀγὼ πρὸς ταῦτα· Οὐ δοκεῖ σοι ἐπὶ Ἰησοῦν, τὸν τοῦ Ναυῆ, τὸν διαδεξάμενον τὴν λαοηγησίαν μετὰ Μωσέα. τὸ αὐτὸ γεγονέναι, ὅτε ἐρρέθη τῷ Μωσεῖ ἐπιθεῖναι τῷ Ἰησοῦ τὰς χεῖρας , εἰπόντος αὐτοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ· Κἀγὼ μεταθήσω ἀπὸ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἐν σοὶ ἐπ᾿ αὐτόν ; Κἀκεῖνος· Μάλιστα. Ὡς οὖν, φημί. ἔτι ὄντος τότε ἐν ἀνθρώποις τοῦ Μωσέως, μετέθηκεν ἐπὶ τὸν Ἰησοῦν ὁ θεὸς ἀπὸ τοῦ ἐν Μωσεῖ πνεύματος, οὕτως καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ Ἡλίου ἐπὶ τὸν Ἰωάννην ἐλθεῖν ὁ θεὸς δυνατὸς ἦν ποιῆσαι. ἵνα, ὥσπερ ὁ Χριστὸς τῇ πρώτῃ παρουσίᾳ ἄδοξος ἐφάνη, οὕτως καὶ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἐν Ἡλίᾳ πάντοτε καθαρεύοντος, ὡς τοῦ Χριστοῦ. ἄδοξος ἡ πρώτη παρουσία νοηθῇ. Κρυφίᾳ γὰρ χειρὶ ὁ κύριος πολεμεῖν τὸν Ἀμαλὴκ εἴρηται , καὶ ὅτι ἔπεσεν ὁ Ἀμαλὴκ οὐκ ἀρνήσεσθε. Εἰ δὲ ἐν τῇ ἐνδόξῳ παρουσίᾳ τοῦ Χριστοῦ πολεμηθήσεσθαι τὸν Ἀμαλὴκ μόνον λέγεται, ποῖος καρπὸς ἔσται τοῦ λόγου. ὅς φησι· Κρυφίᾳ χειρὶ ὁ θεὸς πολεμεῖ τὸν Ἀμαλὴκ: Νοῆσαι δύνασθε ὅτι κρυφία δύναμις τοῦ θεοῦ γέγονε τῷ σταυρωθέντι Χριστῷ, ὃν καὶ τὰ δαιμόνια φρίσσει καὶ πᾶσαι ἁπλῶς αἱ ἀρχαὶ καὶ ἐξουσίαι τῆς γῆς.
thought_title: Trypho and Justin Discuss Christ and Elijah
pass_a_gloss: And Trypho said, It seems to me that those who say he was a man and was chosen and anointed and became Christ are more persuasive than you who say these things; for we all expect the Christ to be born a man from men, and for Elijah to anoint him when he comes. But if this one is the Christ, it is necessary to know that he was born a man from men in every way. But since Elijah has not come, I do not think this one is he. And I again asked him, Does not the word say through Zechariah that Elijah will come before the great and fearful day of the Lord? And he answered, Yes. If then the word compels us to agree that two comings of Christ were prophesied, one in which he will appear suffering and inglorious and unknown, and the other in which he will come glorious and as judge of all, as has been shown in many of the things previously spoken, shall we not think that the word of God announced Elijah would come before the fearful and great day, that is, the second coming of Christ? He answered, Yes. And our Lord, I said, handed down this very thing in his teachings, saying that Elijah would come; and we know that this will happen when our Lord Jesus Christ is about to come in glory from heaven. For the spirit of God that was in Elijah went before him in John, who was a prophet in your nation, after whom no other prophet appeared among you; who, sitting by the Jordan river, cried out, I baptize you in water for repentance, but the one who is stronger than me is coming, whose sandals I am not worthy to carry; he will baptize you in holy spirit and fire. Whose winnowing fan is in his hand, and he will clear his threshing floor and gather the wheat into the storehouse, but the chaff he will burn with unquenchable fire. And your king Herod had thrown this prophet into prison. And when the day of his birthday was being celebrated, and his sister's daughter was dancing pleasingly for him, he said to her, Ask for whatever you want. And the girl's mother suggested that she ask for the head of John, who was in prison; and when she asked, he sent and ordered the head of John to be brought on a platter. Therefore, our Christ also said to those who said Elijah must come before Christ, Elijah will come and restore all things; but I say to you that Elijah has already come, and they did not recognize him, but did to him whatever they wanted. And it is written that Then the disciples understood that he spoke to them about John the Baptist. And Trypho said, You seem to me to be saying something paradoxical, that the prophetic spirit of God that was in Elijah also came to be in John. And I said to him, Does it not seem to you that the same thing happened with Joshua, the son of Nun, who succeeded Moses in leadership, when it was said to Moses to lay his hands on Joshua, and God said, Shall I not put upon him the spirit that is in you? And he said, Yes. As, I say, when Moses was still alive, God transferred the spirit that was in Moses to Joshua, so also God was able to bring the spirit from Elijah to John, so that, just as the first coming of Christ was inglorious, so also the first coming of the spirit that was always in Elijah might be thought inglorious, just like Christ. For it is said that the Lord fought against Amalek with a hidden hand, and you will not deny that Amalek fell. But if in the glorious coming of Christ it is said that only Amalek will be fought, what is the fruit of the word that says, The Lord fights Amalek with a hidden hand? You can see that the hidden power of God became the crucified Christ, whom even the demons fear and all the authorities and powers of the earth.

choices.why: The verb ἐπίστασθαι is used to indicate knowledge or understanding.
The adjective κρυφία is used to describe something that is not visible or apparent.
The noun ἐξουσίαι is used to refer to authorities or powers.

bible_refs.note: The prophet Zechariah is mentioned as the source of a prophecy about Elijah.

pass_b_english: Trypho responded, "It seems to me that those who claim he was a human being, chosen and anointed, and thus became the Christ, are making a more persuasive case than you are. After all, we all expect the Christ to be born a man from men, and for Elijah to come and anoint him. But if this man is the Christ, one must know in every way that he was born a human being from humans. Since Elijah has not come, however, I conclude that this man is not the Christ." I then questioned him further: "Does not the Scripture say through Zechariah that Elijah will come before the great and fearful day of the Lord?" (Zechariah). He answered, "Certainly." "If, then, the Word compels us to acknowledge that two comings of Christ were prophesied—one in which he will appear suffering, inglorious, and unknown, and another in which he will come in glory as the judge of all, as has been demonstrated in many of our previous discussions—should we not understand that the Word of God announced Elijah as a forerunner before that fearful and great day, that is, before the second coming of Christ?" He replied, "Certainly."

"Our Lord," I continued, "handed down this very teaching in his doctrines, declaring that Elijah would come. We know this will take place when our Lord Jesus Christ is about to arrive in glory from heaven. The Spirit of God that was in Elijah went before him in John, a prophet who arose in your nation; after him, no other prophet appeared among you. Sitting by the Jordan River, John cried out, 'I baptize you with water for repentance, but the one who is stronger than I is coming, whose sandals I am not worthy to carry. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire. His winnowing fork is in his hand, and he will clear his threshing floor and gather his wheat into the barn, but the chaff he will burn with unquenchable fire.' Your king Herod threw this prophet into prison. When Herod's birthday was celebrated and the daughter of his sister danced in a way that pleased him, he promised to give her whatever she asked. Prompted by her mother, she requested the head of John the Baptist, who was in prison. Herod sent an executioner and ordered John's head to be brought on a platter. Therefore, our Christ also spoke to those who insisted that Elijah must come before the Christ: 'Elijah will indeed come and restore all things; but I tell you that Elijah has already come, and they did not recognize him, but did to him whatever they pleased.' And it is written, 'Then the disciples understood that he was speaking to them about John the Baptist.'"

Trypho objected, "You seem to me to be saying something paradoxical: that the prophetic Spirit of God that was in Elijah also came to be in John." I answered, "Does it not seem to you that the very same thing happened with Joshua son of Nun, who succeeded Moses in leadership? When God told Moses to lay his hands on Joshua, he said, 'Shall I not put upon him the Spirit that is in you?' (Numbers 11:25). He agreed. Just as God transferred the Spirit that was in Moses to Joshua while Moses was still alive, so also God was able to bring the Spirit from Elijah to John. This was so that, just as the first coming of Christ was inglorious, the first coming of the Spirit that was always in Elijah might also be understood as inglorious, like Christ's. For it is said that the Lord fought against Amalek with a hidden hand, and you will not deny that Amalek fell. But if the Scripture says that Amalek will be fought only in the glorious coming of Christ, what fruit does the word have that says, 'The Lord fights Amalek with a hidden hand'? You can perceive that the hidden power of God became the crucified Christ, whom even the demons fear, and all the authorities and powers of the earth."

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the dialogue between Justin and Trypho. All clauses in the Greek are accounted for in both Pass A and Pass B. Scripture citations (Zechariah and Numbers 11:25) are correctly identified and added as required. The distinction between the two comings of Christ and the analogy of Moses/Joshua and Elijah/John are preserved.
